value.0: Unmoving Center isn't a lesson anymore. It's just how you stand now. Keep it that way when the wind picks up.
You still need the wind to tell you where to stand. Come back when you don't.

You're still moving. Even standing still, you're moving. Six adepts drill wrong at Anchorhead Canyon Range on Tatooine, mistaking fidgeting for stillness. Put six of them down and bring me their canyon range tally, so I know it was you and not the wind.
Take the range key. Six adepts, one tally. Go.

The staff doesn't move. Everything moves around it. That's the whole trick: find the point that doesn't have to go anywhere, and let the fight orbit it. Most people spend years hunting motion. I'm done hunting.
Anchorhead Canyon Range, out past the town, on Tatooine. I've cleared you through the range gate. That key opens it, nothing else will.
Adepts, mostly. They still lean on their weight when they swing. You'll feel the wrongness in it before you see it.
Six adepts. One tally. Anchorhead Canyon Range hasn't moved, and neither should you until it's done.
Six down, and the tally to prove it. Let's see it.
Recorded. The first stillness holds. Rest today; tomorrow the range gets harder to fool.

The adepts were noise. Now go measure the ones who think they've already arrived. Five specialists down at the range mistake rigidity for stillness; they lock up and call it calm. Put five of them down and bring me their sightline calibrator. I want to see how far off their aim really was.
Five specialists, one calibrator. You know the gate.
Rigidity isn't stillness. Rigid things shatter first. These specialists hold a pose and call it mastery. I've watched three of them crack under a first real hit. That's what you're going to test.
Same gate, same key, same Anchorhead Canyon Range. Go further in this time; the specialists don't drill at the entrance.
Better footwork than the adepts, worse instincts. They've drilled the shapes long enough to look convincing at a glance.
Five specialists. One sightline calibrator. Anchorhead Canyon Range is exactly where you left it.
Five down, and their calibrator in your hand. Show me.
Recorded. You're not fidgeting either, not yet. Keep that.

Now the one who runs the floor. Go to Anchorhead Canyon Range, on Tatooine, and put the warden down. Bring me her shattered range crest after. Don't go alone. She has outlasted stronger arms than yours, each one standing by itself.
Bring two who can be still when you cannot. The warden won't care that you came alone.

It demands you stop flinching before the hit lands, not after. The warden never flinches. That's not a boast. I've watched her take a hit that should have ended her and just kept standing. That's the discipline working, or it's something else wearing the discipline's face.
The warden doesn't patrol. She waits at the center of the floor for someone stupid enough to walk to her.

Bring company. Stillness holds when someone else is drawing the storm toward them instead of you. That's the only reason I send you with two others instead of alone. The warden won't wait for you to be ready.
The warden's still standing at Anchorhead Canyon Range. Go back with company, and don't come back without her crest.
The warden's down and you're still standing. Let's see the crest.
Recorded. That's the first proof I didn't expect to see. Don't let it go to your head; the ones after her are worse.

Four of them run the inner ring now. Her students, once. They drill the same stillness and call it a circle so no one has to stand alone in it. Go back to Anchorhead Canyon Range, put down all four, and bring me the marshal's challenge chit they've been trading between themselves like a trophy.
Four of them, one chit. Bring people who can watch your back while you watch theirs.

It demands you let go of the circle they've built around each other. Four of them stand back to back and call that unity. It's just four people afraid to be still alone. I never needed the other three.
Same range. They've claimed the inner floor for themselves, like it belongs to them because they showed up together.
Four means four angles at once. Bring your own circle, or you'll spend the whole fight turning.
The inner circle's still holding the floor at Anchorhead Canyon Range. Four down, one chit, then you're done there.
All four, and their chit besides. You've earned a look at it.
Recorded. There's one lesson left, and it isn't mine to give lightly. Rest first.

The master's the reason I stopped teaching this to anyone who asked. She found the same stillness I did and never came back out of it. She hasn't taken a step in years, they say, and she doesn't need to anymore. Go to Anchorhead Canyon Range and end that. Don't go alone. Nobody has walked away from her circle by themselves, not once.
Bring your two. I'll be waiting for word either way.

It demands you understand what I'm asking you to end. She found the center and never left it. That's not victory, whatever it looks like from outside. I want you to stop her before stillness finishes swallowing her the rest of the way, or before she does the same to you.
Same range, same gate, all the way to the back of it: the one place on that floor that's never moved, and neither has she.

Everything you're learning to do, she already does without trying. That's what I'm sending you to stand against, and why I'm telling you plainly: don't stand against it alone. Bring two you'd trust with your back. She's earned every one of the people who didn't.
She's still standing at Anchorhead Canyon Range, however she's standing. Go back when you have company.
She's not standing anymore. That's all the proof I need. Tell me it's done.
Recorded. The Unmoving Center is yours now, not mine, not hers. Try not to let it swallow you the way it did her.
Anyway, the job.
Six adepts. I can do that.
What's this stillness supposed to be, exactly?
Where do I find them?
What am I walking into?
Not yet.
Here's your tally.
Anyway, the job.
Five specialists, then.
What makes them different from the adepts?
Same range?
What should I watch for this time?
I need a moment.
Here's the calibrator.
Back to it.
I'll bring people. Where's the warden?
What's different about the warden?
Where do I find her?
How many should I bring?
Give me time to find the right two.
Her crest. We got her.
Back to it.
I'll gather my circle.
Who are they to you?
Where's their floor?
How many should I bring this time?
Let me find four I trust first.
Their chit. All four are down.
Back to it.
I'll bring two. Tell me where she is.
What am I actually ending?
Where does she wait?
What is she going to do?
I need to find two people who'd walk in there with me.
It's done. She's not standing.
